steps.caption: Click Guard
steps.narration: This is Click Guard. It records the visits your ads bring in and shows you who keeps coming back.

steps.caption: Pick the website
steps.narration: Pick the website at the top. This roofing company protects three.

steps.caption: Visits, blocked, unique
steps.narration: For the range you pick, the Dashboard counts visits, blocked IPs and unique visitors.

steps.caption: Threat level
steps.narration: Threat level is the share of those visits that were flagged.

steps.caption: Traffic signals
steps.narration: Choose Traffic signals to see what was flagged and what was blocked.

steps.caption: Blocked IPs, with the reason
steps.narration: Blocked IPs lists each address with its reason, and whether it was blocked automatically or by you.

steps.caption: Block an IP yourself
steps.narration: Type an address here and choose Block to add one yourself.

steps.caption: Clicks report
steps.narration: Below, the Clicks report lists every visit: its IP, device, browser, page and status.

steps.caption: Domain settings
steps.narration: Domain settings holds your websites, the IPs you always exclude and the ones you whitelist.

steps.caption: Each website's numbers
steps.narration: Each website shows its visits, unique visitors, blocked IPs and flagged visits.

steps.caption: Google Ads script
steps.narration: Google Ads script is where the list goes to work.

steps.caption: Ready to sync
steps.narration: It shows how many IPs are ready to sync, against Google's limit of five hundred per campaign.

steps.caption: One script, your own account
steps.narration: You paste one script into your own Google Ads account and schedule it. No sign-in is shared.

steps.caption: Menu: Click Guard
steps.narration: You'll find Click Guard first in the rail of the Google Ads tool, on the left.

youtube.title: How to use Click Guard | ConstructHUB
youtube.description: A tour of Click Guard in ConstructHUB: the Dashboard with visits, blocked IPs and the threat level, the Traffic signals page with blocked addresses and their reasons, Domain settings for your exclusion rules, and the Google Ads script that applies the list inside your own Google Ads account.
